intent_summary: An opt-in versioned forecast extension exposes native historical point and pattern evidence from the same frozen historical analysis.

criteria.criterion: One forecast call reuses its historical analysis and returns typed native signed reference, residual, score, triggers, maturity, calibration support, availability and detector provenance in original input positions; explicit recent-level selection is frozen before calibration, whose residuals and readiness use that selected baseline rather than the current forward fit.
criteria.notes: Reviewed single-analysis reuse and matching selected-baseline calibration/readiness; independent include-mode residual/scale replay matches native scores. Native settings disclose the frozen baseline.

criteria.criterion: Frozen-origin earlier point evidence and first-detection pattern snapshots survive changed or appended suffixes; provisional evidence cannot trigger, and retrospective screening is separate from anomaly qualification.
criteria.notes: Both legacy and recent-level tests preserve earlier point-time rows and first-detection patterns. Calibration exclusions remain separately cutoff-annotated operations, not incident labels.

criteria.criterion: Opt-in defaults preserve existing forecast arrays, signed decomposition, horizon prefixes and adjustment semantics; missing gaps and budget failures return unavailable without fabricated or partial evidence.
criteria.notes: Default legacy behavior and standalone recipes remain unchanged. Explicit seasonal/trend outputs, horizon prefixes, partial tails and unavailable failures are covered; recent-level changes only with explicit config.

criteria.criterion: Public schemas, a single-call compatibility adapter and migration guidance document independent selectors, baseline labels, explicit materiality and version negotiation without changing Guard or saved notifications.
criteria.notes: Reviewed additive optional schema/settings fields, exact 0.8.0 bridge guard, independent method/outlier controls, real step lag, versioned caches and retention of old finding provenance. UsageTap implementation is a separate post-publication task.

verification_evidence: Primary Codex agent self-review of the changed behavior and declared references; this is not independent delegated approval.
Python 3.12.9 full source suite: 435 passed in 58.73s with --basetemp=.tmp/pytest-080-release; default system TEMP denied access, so no product change was made for that environment issue.
After the reference-performance optimization and final bridge tests: 24 focused recent-level/evaluation tests passed in 8.66s, including exact equivalence to the existing robust reference policy.
Nested evaluation reproduces all 76 baseline/policy rows across 19 deterministic anonymous fixtures; losses for one stationary seed and a recent real step are retained.
Public demo, agentic demo, distribution demo and installed-API smoke checks passed. Private replay remained only in ignored .tmp and never entered published evidence.

Clean Python 3.12.9 wheel and sdist installs outside checkout passed Guard/forecast/native smoke, dependency/entry-point checks and all 56 native/recent-level regressions per artifact. Max-size bridge smoke covers both legacy and new baseline paths; tag CI must repeat on Linux.
remaining_gaps: Release 0.8.0 must pass tag CI on Python 3.11-3.13 and the offline Linux/Python 3.12 Lambda bundle before publication; local preflight does not certify publication.
Synthetic selection and retrospective local replay do not establish production accuracy. Separately validate UsageTap adoption and retain Current comparison/Guard provenance.
